4.speaker: Player_Romus
4.text: "The violence you mention is the responsibility of a select few individuals. They are being dealt with."

5.speaker: Player_Romus
5.text: "I don't understand. I and my kingdom have been nothing but cooperative in the wake of the Zille incident."

6.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
6.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn01_ZilleVisit_HostileSpeech"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleBombApology"] == false) or Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DefendSO"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_Neutral"] == true

7.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
7.text: "Arguably, it was your aggressive speech that incited the violence in Zille."

8.speaker: Player_Romus
8.text: "Please, just tell me. What can I do to reassure you of your citizens' safety?"

9.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
9.text: "Now you're concerned for my citizens' safety?"
9.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn01_ZilleVisit_HostileSpeech"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Wehlen_ApologizeForSpeech"] == false) or Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DefendSO"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_Neutral"] == true

13.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
13.text: "You may not have incited the incident, but by failing to denounce the suspected perpetrators, you condoned it."

14.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
14.text: "I cannot simply hand these people's lives over to a government that is, at best, indifferent to their existence. Who will protect them?"

15.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
15.text: "We've therefore drafted an addendum to the original treaty. A series of measures meant to renew our old friendship."

16.speaker: Player_Romus
16.text: "And if this 'friendship' helps Wehlen bypass certain trade sanctions, so much the better."

17.speaker: Player_Romus
17.text: "Whatever you believe Rumburg has done or is doing to Wehlen, Rizia has absolutely no part in it."

22.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
22.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn01_ZilleVisit_HostileSpeech"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleBombApology"] == false) or Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DefendSO"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_Neutral"] == true

28.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
28.text: "I do not take issue with your response to the incident, Your Majesty."
28.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn01_ZilleVisit_HostileSpeech"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleBombApology"] == false) or Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DefendSO"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_Neutral"] == true) == false

29.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
29.text: "But your partnership with Rumburg, despite all of its efforts to destabilize us, is a warning sign to me."

30.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
30.text: "I cannot simply hand these people's lives over to the friend of my enemy."

31.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
31.text: "Your continued partnership with Rumburg, in the face of all its efforts to destabilize us, is also a warning sign to me."

32.speaker: Player_Romus
32.text: "I understand. We will make a special effort to integrate all Wehzeks who wish to stay."

33.speaker: Player_Romus
33.text: "They don't need protecting, because they never belonged in Zille in the first place."

37.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
37.text: "His Majesty is trying to say that Rizia takes Wehlen's concerns very seriously."

39.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
39.text: "All we can do is take every available measure to ensure the security of Zille's Wehzek population once the region is back in Rizia's hands."

40.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
40.text: "That is comforting to know, Mr. Esquibel."

45.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
45.text: "As you may know, Wehlen has found itself with an oil surplus due to decreased demand from Rumburg and other monarchies."

46.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
46.text: "We therefore propose a straightforward exchange of Wehzek oil for Rizian gold. At what I am sure you'll agree is a very favorable rate."

47.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
47.text: "And we are ready to take all available measures to ensure the security of your people once the region is back in Rizia's hands."

48.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
48.text: "My ministers and I agree that before Zille is reintegrated into Rizia, a good-faith effort must be made to strengthen the bonds between our countries."

52.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
52.text: "Of course I was pleased that the individuals responsible for the attack were found and brought forward so quickly. Almost too quickly."

53.speaker: Player_Romus
53.text: "Wehlen is our direct neighbor and our historical ally. We will always prioritize relations with your country over Rumburg."

56.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
56.text: "For instance, we're seeking to expand the market for morphine and other pharmaceutical products, not to mention Merkopa's finest tobacco."

57.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
57.text: "Four barrels for every ounce, to be exact."

58.speaker: Player_Romus
58.text: "Why would Rizia need drugs from Wehlen? We have our own pharmaceutical companies."

59.speaker: Player_Romus
59.text: "The Queen Mother always spoke highly of Wehzek tobacco."

61.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
61.text: "If there's one fact everyone knows about Wehlen, it's that we sell oil."

68.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
68.text: "Six barrels for every ounce, to be exact."

69.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
69.text: "Eight barrels for every ounce, to be exact."

72.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
72.text: "We do have other interested parties. But of course, Rizia gets first priority."

73.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
73.text: "I beg your pardon, Your Majesty, but are you keeping up with current exchange rates? Other countries can only dream of a deal this good."

74.speaker: Player_Romus
74.text: "What makes you think that Rizia is in the market for Wehzek oil, President Smolak?"

75.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
75.text: "Everyone is in the market for oil. There's a reason that they call it 'black gold'."

76.speaker: Player_Romus
76.text: "An interesting offer. And the rate is indeed favorable."

77.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
77.text: "I should tell you that Wehlen has other commodities too, Mr. Esquibel."

78.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
78.text: "If the price is right, why not? I'm a flexible man."

79.speaker: Narrator
79.text: With a grin, he held his arm up and bent his wrist nearly all the way backwards. Laurento smiled patiently.

80.speaker: Narrator
80.text: Just ahead of my meeting with him, I convened with my council for a briefing. Hugo knocked on the table to begin.

81.speaker: Hugo Toras
81.text: "Thank you all for joining us here."

82.speaker: Narrator
82.text: He looked around the table at Vina, Laurento, Lucita, Elena, Sal and Titus.

86.speaker: Narrator
86.text: He looked around the table at Vina, Laurento, Lucita, Elena and Sal.

87.speaker: Hugo Toras
87.text: "Laurento, as you have the latest information from Wehlen's foreign ministry, would you like to begin? What can His Majesty expect today?"

88.speaker: Narrator
88.text: Laurento stood up. He paced back and forth energetically as he spoke.

89.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
89.text: "We are in uncharted territory, Your Grace."

90.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
90.text: "President Smolak's invocation of the Threat Mitigation Protocol has been challenged, but the AN failed to meet a consensus. Essentially, he is in a position to hold Zille hostage until his demands are met."

91.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
91.text: "Lespia's statement of support for us at the AN has further increased international pressure."

98.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
98.text: "Most crucially, the two men who have admitted responsibility for the Zille attack are in Wehzek custody. Which doesn't negate President Smolak's claim that security has been compromised, but does weaken it."
98.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Lespia_WehlenHelp"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Wehlen_Scapegoats"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Zille_ATAActive"] == true) == false)

105.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
105.text: "Our investigators are cooperating with Wehlen intelligence, which will make it more difficult for President Smolak to claim we are uninterested in the region's security."

113.speaker: Player_Romus
113.text: "Ms. Werner, which resources are we able to bargain with?"

114.speaker: Player_Romus
114.text: "Hugo, is there any word from the House of Delegates on this?"

118.speaker: Narrator
118.text: He looked around the table at Laurento, Lucita, Elena, Sal and Titus.

122.speaker: Narrator
122.text: He looked around the table at Laurento, Lucita, Elena and Sal.

123.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
123.text: "Even so, we should handle this meeting with delicacy. Any aggression on our part can be used against us."
123.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Lespia_WehlenHelp"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Wehlen_Scapegoats"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn04_WehlenInvestigation_Cooperate"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Zille_ATAActive"] == true) == false)

124.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
124.text: "The presence of the Ariana Toras Association in Zille has helped sway public sentiment to our side."

128.speaker: Player_Romus
128.text: "To hell with delicacy. Wehlen's never been delicate with us."

129.speaker: Player_Romus
129.text: "I'm prepared to give President Smolak everything he asks for."

130.speaker: Player_Romus
130.text: "Delicacy is one thing. Submission is another. We must be careful what we promise."

131.speaker: Hugo Toras
131.text: "Very true, Your Majesty. At some point, it may become necessary to call Wehlen's bluff."

132.speaker: Hugo Toras
132.text: "Very generous, Your Majesty. But at some point, it may become necessary to call Wehlen's bluff."

133.speaker: Hugo Toras
133.text: "This is true, Mr. Esquibel. At some point, it may become necessary to call Wehlen's bluff."

134.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
134.text: "I know this much, Your Grace. Unless concessions are made, it will take years if not decades to get Zille back."

137.speaker: Sal Ignacius
137.text: "Our neighbor has long followed the path of Dastnurity, and I do not fault them for it."

138.speaker: Sal Ignacius
138.text: "But in the hands of the current regime, that religion has become a cudgel with which to persecute Wehlen's Golcondist minority."

140.speaker: Elena Werner
140.text: "Gold is always an option. Especially since we raised our stake in RRG."

147.speaker: Elena Werner
147.text: "Gold production has slowed since the latest regulations were implemented, but it's still an option."
147.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Economy_RaiseRRGStake"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Welfare_WorkersRightsAllIndustries"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Resources_Budget"] < 1) == false)

149.speaker: Elena Werner
149.text: "Although if you follow through with your support of Morella and its crusade for control of the Meftiem ITZ, one of our most lucrative sources may soon be off-limits."

153.speaker: Elena Werner
153.text: "And despite our deal with the Sords, we have a small wine surplus that we can sell or trade."

157.speaker: Elena Werner
157.text: "And we have a sizeable wine surplus that we can sell or trade."

161.speaker: Elena Werner
161.text: "The regulations have also dented our small arms industry, but we can offer Dator rifles."
161.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Morella_ANSpeech_SideWith"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Welfare_WorkersRightsAllIndustries"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Welfare_WorkersRightsAllExceptMining"] == true)

162.speaker: Elena Werner
162.text: "If it's weapons that Wehlen is interested in, we can offer our Dator rifles."
162.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Morella_ANSpeech_SideWith"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Welfare_WorkersRightsAllIndustries"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Welfare_WorkersRightsAllExceptMining"] == true) == false)

163.speaker: Elena Werner
163.text: "We didn't drink it all in Qalus. It only felt like we did."

167.speaker: Narrator
167.text: Vina grimaced at the reminder while the other councilors chuckled.

169.speaker: Narrator
169.text: I glanced over at Lucita, who threw me a wink. The others didn't seem to notice.

173.speaker: Narrator
173.text: My face grew heated as I thought about that night. The others didn't seem to notice.

180.speaker: Elena Werner
180.text: "*If* we can manage to free up the natural gas in the Aureus field in time, that will be a tradeable asset."

185.speaker: Elena Werner
185.text: "But a country as rich in oil as Wehlen won't need much of it."

191.speaker: Lucita Azaro
191.text: "A few fingerprints were found near the bomb site, but they don't match any of the ones we have on file for Su Omina members."

192.speaker: Lucita Azaro
192.text: "Nor were they recognized by Wehlen's database."

196.speaker: Lucita Azaro
196.text: "There's a chance they could be Wehzek. We don't have access to Wehlen's database."

197.speaker: Hugo Toras
197.text: "But that's good for us. It means Su Omina can be ruled out."

198.speaker: Lucita Azaro
198.text: "Not entirely. We don't have files for every single member."

202.speaker: Lucita Azaro
202.text: "And it hasn't helped that pamphlets bearing the group's logo have surfaced in Zille recently."

205.speaker: Titus Gordion
205.text: "We know certain individuals on Su Omina's fringes have planned and carried out isolated acts of violence."

206.speaker: Titus Gordion
206.text: "But there is nothing connecting them to the group's more high-profile members or supporters. Duke Rico Toras, for example."

207.speaker: Hugo Toras
207.text: "But surely their involvement in the Zille incident can be ruled out, then?"

210.speaker: Hugo Toras
210.text: "They have met about it, Your Majesty."

211.speaker: Hugo Toras
211.text: "The majority consensus was that the timeliness of the Zille handover should take a backseat to protecting Rizian interests."

212.speaker: Hugo Toras
212.text: "Conceding too much to Wehlen too quickly will earn you the ire of Baroness de Rava and her party."

213.speaker: Hugo Toras
213.text: "The opposition, meanwhile, is much more amenable to compromise. Particularly those party members from Brenas."

221.speaker: Titus Gordion
221.text: "And a set of fingerprints sent by Wehlen intelligence did not match any of the members we have on file."

223.speaker: Titus Gordion
223.text: "These people are better organized than they seem at first glance. They may well be hiding something."

227.speaker: Lucita Azaro
227.text: "Wehlen intelligence sent us a set of fingerprints to run through our database. There were no matches."

228.speaker: Lucita Azaro
228.text: "Wehlen intelligence claimed they found a set of fingerprints that did not belong to any Wehzek citizen on file."

229.speaker: Lucita Azaro
229.text: "They claimed the prints didn't belong to any Wehzek citizen on file, but without our own presence up there, we have no way of verifying that."

230.speaker: Lucita Azaro
230.text: "Of course, without our own presence up there, we have no way of verifying that."

231.speaker: Hugo Toras
231.text: "But no additional evidence has been found that points to the involvement of Su Omina."

232.speaker: Lucita Azaro
232.text: "No. Well, maybe. Apparently pamphlets bearing the group's logo have been surfacing in Zille recently."

236.speaker: Lucita Azaro
236.text: "No, they still haven't been either fully implicated or fully ruled out."

241.speaker: Elena Werner
241.text: "If all else fails, we have a healthy budget. But I'd rather not pay Wehlen what amounts to ransom money."
241.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Lucita_Together"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Pabel_Together"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Cede"] == true) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Resources_Budget"] > 3)

242.speaker: Elena Werner
242.text: "They may flat-out ask us to buy their goods instead of trade. But we should be careful with our budget, and anyway, I'd rather not pay Wehlen what amounts to ransom money."
242.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Lucita_Together"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Pabel_Together"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Cede"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Resources_Budget"] > 3) == false)

243.speaker: Vina Toras
243.text: "That makes sense. They've been missing a piece of their province for long enough already."

247.speaker: Hugo Toras
247.text: "With all due respect, Your Highness, the Sazons lost the right to call Zille 'theirs' when the former Duke of Iza committed his act of treachery."

248.speaker: Hugo Toras
248.text: "They cannot seriously expect that it will be re-incorporated into Brenas as if nothing happened."

249.speaker: Hugo Toras
249.text: "And what makes you think they deserve it, Mr. Esquibel? Should they be rewarded for harboring traitors?"

250.speaker: Vina Toras
250.text: "And why not? We took Iza from them. How much more punishment does their house need to endure?"

251.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
251.text: "As a son of Brenas myself, I agree with Her Highness. Zille is home to many ancestral estates of the Sazons, not to mention the Esquibels."

252.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
252.text: "That makes sense. The people of Brenas have awaited the return of their ancestral land for long enough."

272.speaker: Player_Romus
272.text: "I'm as briefed as I'm going to be. Time to go meet President Smolak."

273.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
273.text: "Very good, Your Majesty. He's expecting us in the downstairs diplomatic suite."

274.speaker: Player_Romus
274.text: "What fallout can we expect if we don't come to an agreement?"
274.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Zille_SuOminaActive"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_CouncilBriefWehlen_Investigation"] == true  and  (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_CouncilBriefWehlen_Delegates"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_CouncilBriefWehlen_Religion"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_CouncilBriefWehlen_Trade"] == true)) and (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_CouncilBriefing_BackupPlan"] == false)

276.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
276.text: "I highly doubt that a full deal will be reached today. Only the beginnings of one."

277.speaker: Lucita Azaro
277.text: "His Majesty's question stands. Do we have a contingency plan?"

278.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
278.text: "Well, Duchess, if our negotiations fall through, and international pressure is insufficient to force Wehlen back to the table..."

279.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
279.text: "Then the responsibility will fall on Zille itself."

281.speaker: Narrator
281.text: Lucita flashed him a skeptical look.

282.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
282.text: "If a majority of Zille's citizens believe the territory should belong to Rizia, the Wehzek government cannot simply ignore them, especially if we gather external support."

283.speaker: Lucita Azaro
283.text: "They can and they will. No state peacefully gives power away."

284.speaker: Player_Romus
284.text: "That's true. We're a monarchy. Supporting any kind of people's movement could backfire horribly."

285.speaker: Player_Romus
285.text: "Do we even have a majority? I thought opinion was divided."

286.speaker: Player_Romus
286.text: "It doesn't have to be peaceful, does it?"

288.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
288.text: "The Zille branch of ATA has already begun coordinating a Rizian-led reunification initiative in the wake of the AN announcement."

290.speaker: Player_Romus
290.text: "Forget I asked. I'd rather focus on negotiations for now."

294.speaker: Lucita Azaro
294.text: "Zille is cut off from the Wehzek mainland. Divert enough funding and weapons to the right groups, and we can make an overthrow happen without getting our hands dirty."

295.speaker: Lucita Azaro
295.text: "President Smolak may not respect a peaceful transition. But he will respect that."

296.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
296.text: "This isn't the same as the '26 uprising. It's the long-suffering citizens of Zille calling for the protection of their king."

297.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
297.text: "President Smolak's announcement has already put many undecided citizens into the pro-Rizian column. And we have avenues to influence them further."

298.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
298.text: "If we opted to fund a Zille branch of the Ariana Toras Association, they could coordinate a Rizian-led reunification initiative."

299.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
299.text: "It doesn't have to be one or the other. In fact, playing on citizens' sentiments could give us a negotiating edge."

303.speaker: Player_Romus
303.text: "I'm in enough trouble with Pales. I just want to get this over with."

304.speaker: Hugo Toras
304.text: "I'm sure President Smolak is going to attempt to use the Pales imbroglio to his advantage. We cannot let him demand too much because of it."

305.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
305.text: "He will respect a peaceful transition if one has officially been called for."

306.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
306.text: "My dear Duchess, you and your family really must learn that bloodshed isn't the answer to everything."

307.speaker: Lucita Azaro
307.text: "Zille doesn't need a referendum, Mr. Esquibel. It needs a resistance."

308.speaker: Lucita Azaro
308.text: "You know what will end in bloodshed? Telling our people in Zille to rise against the government without giving them the means to defend themselves."

309.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
309.text: "With enough pressure from both inside and outside Zille, Wehlen will have to give the region back. Or at the very least hold a referendum."

310.speaker: Lucita Azaro
310.text: "It's cut off from the Wehzek mainland. Divert enough funding and weapons to the right groups, and we can make an overthrow happen without getting our hands dirty."

311.speaker: Player_Romus
311.text: "I think we're in a good position to negotiate Zille's return without any of that."
311.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Zille_SuOminaActive"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DenounceSO"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Security_GoldenGuard_InvestigateSO"] == false) == false)

312.speaker: Player_Romus
312.text: "I see your point, but violence should only be used as a last resort. Otherwise we risk destroying the territory we're trying to gain."
312.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Zille_SuOminaActive"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DenounceSO"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Security_GoldenGuard_InvestigateSO"] == false) == false)

313.speaker: Player_Romus
313.text: "I do place stock in a people's vote. And I don't like the idea of manipulating one."
313.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Zille_SuOminaActive"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DenounceSO"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Security_GoldenGuard_InvestigateSO"] == false) == false)

314.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
314.text: "The Zille branch of ATA has already begun coordinating a Rizian-led reunification initiative in the wake of the AN announcement."

318.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
318.text: "If we opted to fund a Zille branch of the Ariana Toras Association, they could coordinate a Rizian-led reunification initiative."

319.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
319.text: "With enough pressure from both inside and outside Zille, Wehlen will have to give the region back. Or at the very least hold a referendum."

320.speaker: Lucita Azaro
320.text: "Or, for that matter, sending the message that our all-powerful king is placing stock in the results of a people's vote."

321.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
321.text: "We should not support a referendum if we're not prepared to sway Zille in Rizia's favor. The Duchess and I can agree on that."

322.speaker: Lucita Azaro
322.text: "Of course, Your Majesty. But if negotiations fail, things could go south quickly. We should be prepared."

330.speaker: Narrator
330.text: Elena and Hugo left the room. Lucita seemed to be intentionally delaying her exit. Her eyes locked on to mine.
330.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Lucita_Together"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Lucita_PromisedDate"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true) == false)

334.speaker: Lucita Azaro
334.text: "Don't forget there's always a back-up plan."

337.speaker: Narrator
337.text: Titus and Laurento stood by the door, waiting to escort me to the meeting.

338.speaker: Player_Romus
338.text: "Can you two wait outside? I'll be there in a moment."

339.speaker: Narrator
339.text: Titus, Laurento and I walked through the palace's winding corridors until we reached the first-floor diplomatic suite.

341.speaker: Narrator
341.text: With a knowing grin, Laurento bowed and motioned for Titus to follow him into the hall.

343.speaker: Narrator
343.text: Lucita snapped her attache case shut and turned to me.

344.speaker: Player_Romus
344.text: "I hope you understand that our personal relationship has no bearing on my political decisions."

348.speaker: Player_Romus
348.text: "Here? In the council chambers? And right before a diplomatic meeting? Well, if you insist."

349.speaker: Player_Romus
349.text: "Sorry I haven't taken you on that date yet."

350.speaker: Player_Romus
350.text: "Whatever you have to say, make it fast."

352.speaker: Lucita Azaro
352.text: "No need to apologize. In fact, I've been thinking."

353.speaker: Narrator
353.text: Lucita laughed and shook her head.

354.speaker: Narrator
354.text: She held out her hand. In it was a small wooden object.

356.speaker: Lucita Azaro
356.text: "Of course, Your Majesty. In fact, I've been thinking."

359.speaker: Narrator
359.text: It was a chess piece -- a queen. It appeared to be made of marble with golden details.

360.speaker: Narrator
360.text: I picked it up and took a closer look. There was a pair of crossed swords carved into it. The Azaro sigil.

361.speaker: Lucita Azaro
361.text: "My uncle's. The mutineers ransacked his country house after they killed him. They took the set, but this must have fallen out in the chaos."

362.speaker: Player_Romus
362.text: "Thanks to my father's partnership with Wehlen, those killers were brought to justice."

363.speaker: Player_Romus
363.text: "I can't take this. It must hold deep sentimental value for you."

364.speaker: Player_Romus
364.text: "I'm sorry, Lucita. My father should never have let it come to that."

365.speaker: Player_Romus
365.text: "A queen. The most valuable piece on the chessboard."

367.speaker: Lucita Azaro
367.text: "What's done is done. We can only move forward."

368.speaker: Lucita Azaro
368.text: "Keep it as a reminder of what we have to lose. And what we've already lost."

369.speaker: Lucita Azaro
369.text: "Blood for blood. And I'm afraid there's more yet to be spilled."

370.speaker: Lucita Azaro
370.text: "She's a versatile attacker and an invaluable defender. All in the service of protecting her king."

374.speaker: Narrator
374.text: She pulled me into a quick kiss, then lightly shoved me in the direction of the door.

375.speaker: Narrator
375.text: She took my hand and gave it a quick squeeze.

376.speaker: Narrator
376.text: I slipped the chess piece into my pocket and stepped out into the hall to rejoin my bodyguard and foreign councilor.

378.speaker: Lucita Azaro
378.text: "You should head to your meeting. We'll debrief later."

385.speaker: Narrator
385.text: Laurento's face reddened. He didn't speak another word as Titus escorted us through winding corridors to the first-floor diplomatic suite.

387.speaker: Narrator
387.text: We left Titus standing guard outside the door and walked in. President Smolak was in the sitting room, flipping through a copy of the Royal Herald.

388.speaker: Narrator
388.text: He stood up and bowed to each of us.

389.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
389.text: "Your Majesty, Mr. Esquibel! It's truly a pleasure to be here."

390.speaker: Player_Romus
390.text: "The pleasure is mutual, Mr. President. Thank you for meeting me."

391.speaker: Player_Romus
391.text: "I wish I could say the same, President Smolak."

392.speaker: Player_Romus
392.text: "I'm sorry we don't have carpets. I know that's traditional among your people."

393.speaker: Player_Romus
393.text: "President Smolak. I'm glad that you finally found the time to meet with me."

394.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
394.text: "Don't be sorry. We are not among my people, are we?"

395.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
395.text: "And why not? Our differences aside, there is always pleasure in two world leaders meeting eye to eye."

396.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
396.text: "Circumstances have changed since we last met, of course. But I am confident we can come to an understanding."

397.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
397.text: "Yes, I apologize that it's taken so long. Things are quite turbulent in my country, as you understand."

398.speaker: Narrator
398.text: He set down the newspaper he'd been reading.

399.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
399.text: "You wouldn't believe what they're saying about me in your paper, Your Majesty."

400.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
400.text: "'Smolak's iron grip on Zille, enforced by dictatorial command rather than any real respect for international law or the rights of the local population, should be seen as a threat to us all.'"

401.speaker: Player_Romus
401.text: "I don't see anything wrong with that statement."

402.speaker: Player_Romus
402.text: "I can't control what the Rizian press says about you, no more than I can control what it says about me."

403.speaker: Player_Romus
403.text: "That's indeed over the top, Mr. President. I'll ensure that my papers refrain from such slander in the future."

405.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
405.text: "I'd kindly remind you that Zille only became Wehzek territory in the first place because your father asked my predecessor to crush a people's rebellion."

406.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
406.text: "Where was Rizia's respect for the rights of the local population then?"

410.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
410.text: "I wouldn't permit such poison to be spread about me in my own country."

411.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
411.text: "Your Majesty, I have the suspicion that your media functions much in the same way as mine. Not a word is permitted that your government doesn't approve of."

412.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
412.text: "You see, you and I are not as different as you might like to believe."

414.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
414.text: "Relax, Your Majesty. You should read what my country's papers are saying about you!"

416.speaker: Player_Romus
416.text: "That wasn't the same. It was a violent uprising led by criminals."

417.speaker: Player_Romus
417.text: "We cracked down on traitors to the throne. Whereas from what I hear, your country is involved in the persecution of innocents."

418.speaker: Player_Romus
418.text: "You're absolutely right, Mr. President. King Valero should never have asked Wehlen to intervene. "

419.speaker: Player_Romus
419.text: "That's true, Mr. President. Both of us only want what's best for our people. I'm sure we will be able to come to an agreement with that in mind."

420.speaker: Player_Romus
420.text: "You are right. Neither of us want Arcasian greed to spread across Merkopa."

421.speaker: Player_Romus
421.text: "With all due respect, we are. Being a king comes with challenges and pressures that ordinary presidents can never understand."

422.speaker: Player_Romus
422.text: "Mr. President, we live in a global society now. Censoring the press in your own country will only get you labeled as a tyrant by others."

423.speaker: Player_Romus
423.text: "I had my misgivings about it as well. But nothing's really changed. I just gave a few dissenters the opportunity to vent their spleens."

424.speaker: Player_Romus
424.text: "A free press is an important component of a just nation, Mr. Smolak. We leaders must be held to account somehow."

425.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
425.text: "And you are hearing this from whom? Be careful what you believe. A lot of false information is circulating about Wehlen at the moment."

426.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
426.text: "Wehlen also has violent uprisings in its past. If they had not succeeded, I wouldn't be here speaking to you today."

427.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
427.text: "But if he had not, you wouldn't be here speaking to me today. Maybe you wouldn't even be here at all."

428.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
428.text: "Are you really going to label me as a tyrant, *Your Majesty*?"

429.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
429.text: "That's how it starts. But give them enough time, and they'll fill the public's heads with malicious lies."

430.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
430.text: "I thought that was the best part of being a king. No need to be accountable to anyone."

433.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
433.text: "If we cannot understand each other, then what was the point of my coming here today?"

434.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
434.text: "Interesting, Your Majesty. I always thought you monarchies preferred to stay out of the superpower fray."

440.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
440.text: "But your words at the AN indicated otherwise. A king supporting his eastward-leaning neighbors -- who would have thought?"

441.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
441.text: "But Mr. Alvarez's speech at the AN showed a different reality. You claim to be against Arcasian greed, yet you beg one of its biggest figureheads for help?"
441.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Valgsland_AppealToAtANSpeech"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Morella_ANSpeech_SideWith"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Lespia_WehlenHelp"] == true)

446.speaker: Narrator
446.text: I saw relief in Laurento's eyes.

447.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
447.text: "But what do I know? I don't have to worry about such things, because my people love me."

449.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
449.text: "Your family did what it needed to do to stay in power. There's no need to be ashamed of it."

451.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
451.text: "But I don't fault your family for doing what it had to do to stay in power. Who knows? If I were a king, maybe I would have done the same."

453.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
453.text: "King Valero made what he thought was the best decision at the time for his citizens. I'm sure the same applies to you, Mr. President."

454.speaker: Narrator
454.text: He grinned. Laurento jumped in smoothly.

455.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
455.text: "The meeting room should be ready by now. Shall we proceed?"

456.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
456.text: "Who knows? If I were a king, maybe I would have done the same!"

457.speaker: Narrator
457.text: He grinned. Laurento jumped in smoothly.

459.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
459.text: "What His Majesty meant to say was that despite your differing leadership styles, he believes there is still a chance to come to a productive agreement today. And so do I."

462.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
462.text: "Lespia's statement was unprompted, Mr. President. It would have been against AN protocol to interrupt it."

463.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
463.text: "We're already beginning to find common ground. I'm optimistic for these negotiations."

464.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
464.text: "You are correct, Mr. President. As a member of GRACE, our kingdom does not officially support or oppose any superpower."

465.speaker: Narrator
465.text: He led us into the next room over, where a set of blue-upholstered armchairs were arranged around a circular table.

466.speaker: Narrator
466.text: The three of us had a seat. A palace aide came by with water and coffee.

467.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
467.text: "Now that you're here, Mr. Smolak, can you explain in greater detail why you decided to postpone the Zille handover?"

468.speaker: Narrator
468.text: Smolak took a sip of water. He slowly wiped his mustache.

470.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
470.text: "Zille is now home to several million citizens of Wehzek origin. Under the terms of the treaty our predecessors signed, they were to have the right to stay and work in the region."

471.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
471.text: "But the Zille attack made it clear that those terms would not be respected. Without the protection of my government, I fear further violence will come to those who stay."

472.speaker: Player_Romus
472.text: "What about the Rizians whose homes were destroyed by your civil war? You didn't seem to care about their safety."

473.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
473.text: "The war was devastating to Rizians and Wehzeks alike, but you cannot blame me for the mistakes of my predecessor. I have spent the last decade helping my nation recover from that terrible tragedy."

475.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
475.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn01_ZilleVisit_HostileSpeech"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleBombApology"] == false) or Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DefendSO"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_Neutral"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn04_WehlenInvestigation_Cooperate"] == false

476.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
476.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn01_ZilleVisit_HostileSpeech"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleBombApology"] == false) or Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DefendSO"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_Neutral"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn04_WehlenInvestigation_Cooperate"] == false) == false

481.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
481.text: "Your actions, both prior to and in the wake of the Zille incident, have shown your disregard for Wehzek lives."
481.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn01_ZilleVisit_HostileSpeech"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleBombApology"] == false) or Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DefendSO"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_Neutral"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn04_WehlenInvestigation_Cooperate"] == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn01_ZilleVisit_HostileSpeech"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleBombApology"] == false)

482.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
482.text: "You have been nothing but cooperative since the Zille incident, I will grant you that."
482.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn01_ZilleVisit_HostileSpeech"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleBombApology"] == false) or Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DefendSO"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_Neutral"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn04_WehlenInvestigation_Cooperate"] == false) == false

483.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
483.text: "Your actions in the wake of the Zille incident revealed your true feelings about Wehlen and its people."
483.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn01_ZilleVisit_HostileSpeech"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleBombApology"] == false) or Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DefendSO"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_Neutral"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn04_WehlenInvestigation_Cooperate"] == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn01_ZilleVisit_HostileSpeech"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleBombApology"] == false) == false)

484.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
484.text: "Meanwhile, we are worried about the impact the loss of Zille will have on our economy. We will need a way to stabilize our currency."

485.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
485.text: "But do they have access to the largest poppy fields in Merkopa?"

486.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
486.text: "She's right, your mother. A puff of our khisha and a sip of your wine... I can't think of a more delightful combination."

487.speaker: Player_Romus
487.text: "Mr. Smolak, we are negotiating for the legal return of my territory, not haggling in some Wehzek bazaar."

488.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
488.text: "Our timber industry is also unparalleled in Merkopa. Your nobles might take a particular interest in our woodcarvings..."

489.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
489.text: "The morphine my country produces has been used on battlefields across the continent. Wars have been won because of it."

490.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
490.text: "Haggling, negotiating -- either way, it's all about who can offer what and who wants it more. Right, Mr. Esquibel?"

492.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
492.text: "Our artisans only serve the most exclusive customers, Your Majesty. Each piece can take years to complete."

493.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
493.text: "We don't plan on going into battle, President Smolak. But access to lower-cost pharmaceuticals would benefit our health system."

494.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
494.text: "I know shops in Iza's Little Wraclawitz quarter that sell khisha under the table. They can't restock it fast enough."

495.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
495.text: "A few of my family's heirlooms are Wehzek handiwork. They still look good as new after a century."

496.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
496.text: "Indeed, Mr. Esquibel. There is a reason your poorer citizens cross into Zille to buy simple painkillers."

497.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
497.text: "Your Majesty, Mr. Esquibel... how much do you know about the Bludish Freedom Front?"

498.speaker: Player_Romus
498.text: "They were founded in protest of Tarquin Soll's policies in Sordland. They've been active around the border between your countries."

500.speaker: Player_Romus
500.text: "They're a coalition of radical separatists who've lost their purpose since their leader was jailed."

501.speaker: Player_Romus
501.text: "They're a resistance group fighting against the oppression of the Bludish people. They've been forced to commit some extreme acts over their history."

502.speaker: Player_Romus
502.text: "They're a dangerous terror organization whose fight for 'freedom' has cost many innocents their lives."

503.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
503.text: "That may have been how they started. But the threat they pose is not limited to that one small region."

504.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
504.text: "President Smolak, I am aware that the BFF has not gone completely inactive since the retirement of Tarquin Soll. And that they may in fact be gathering their strength."

506.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
506.text: "Dewlen Arge was one head of a many-headed beast. Cutting him off only made the others angrier."

508.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
508.text: "The Bluds have been offered every opportunity to live alongside Wehzeks and Sords. They chose violence instead."

511.speaker: Player_Romus
511.text: "Mr. President, I can't ban people from my country based on their religion."

512.speaker: Player_Romus
512.text: "Rizia is duty-bound to welcome our fellow Wruhecists. Even if they belong to a fringe sect."

513.speaker: Player_Romus
513.text: "I can get behind a Bludish ban. But banning Derdians would have huge international ramifications."

514.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
514.text: "Derdians are a nationality, not a religion. And Wehzek Bluds are an ethnic group as distinctly marked in their identification documents."

515.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
515.text: "This is not about Wruhecism. It is about terrorists and those who support them."

516.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
516.text: "That may be so, Mr. Smolak. But the international community would see this as a religious ban."

517.speaker: Player_Romus
517.text: "Whether Derdian or Bludish, Golcondism is not compatible with Rizian values. That much we can agree on."

518.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
518.text: "As huge as those of granting a safe haven to radical terrorists?"

519.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
519.text: "Mr. Smolak, we are prepared to increase our border security, but an outright ban on Bluds and Derdians will be seen as religious discrimination."

520.speaker: Player_Romus
520.text: "I agree that closer cultural and economic ties could benefit both of our nations."

521.speaker: Player_Romus
521.text: "What precisely do you mean by 'friendship'? A military alliance?"

522.speaker: Player_Romus
522.text: "If you are concerned about Rizian nationalists attacking Wehzek citizens, I must warn you that such measures will only make them more angry."

523.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
523.text: "Not quite. We in Wehlen do not require the Rizian military's help to defend ourselves."

524.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
524.text: "They would indeed. After all, how well can Rumburg look after you when you're so far away from each other?"

525.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
525.text: "Why so cynical, Your Majesty? Our countries were close allies once. They can be again."

526.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
526.text: "If the fate of Wehlen is as closely entwined with Rizia's as my proposal outlines, your nationalists will only be fighting against themselves."

527.speaker: Narrator
527.text: Laurento pulled a folder out of his briefcase and opened it on the table.

528.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
528.text: "Mr. President, we received the draft from your ministers, but the terms were extremely vague. You're asking for a trade deal, a bilateral migration agreement and... a counter-terrorism cooperation pact?"

529.speaker: Player_Romus
529.text: "Tell me more about this trade deal, President Smolak."

530.speaker: Player_Romus
530.text: "I'm interested in hearing more about this anti-terrorism pact."

538.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
538.text: "Your family must have discerning taste. But we can also offer raw timber as well as less deluxe furniture at lower price points."

539.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
539.text: "Then you understand that Wehlen is not only an oil country, just as Rizia is not only a gold one. There is plenty we can offer each other."

541.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
541.text: "But you have not yet made it clear what you want from Rizia."

543.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
543.text: "You may be aware that most Bluds are followers of the Wruhecist sect called Golcondism."

544.speaker: Player_Romus
544.text: "Yes. Their religious fanaticism makes them even more dangerous."

545.speaker: Player_Romus
545.text: "I don't see why their beliefs are important. Their motivations are political, not religious."

546.speaker: Player_Romus
546.text: "So I hear. Aren't they the largest Golcondist community outside of Derdia?"

547.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
547.text: "Their beliefs are important to the Republic of Derdia. Which has been granting sanctuary even to the most notorious of Bludish criminals."

548.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
548.text: "Their beliefs are shared by the Republic of Derdia. Which has been granting sanctuary even to the most notorious of Bludish criminals."

549.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
549.text: "Precisely. And in fact, Jorga Azmal's country has been granting sanctuary even to the most notorious of Bludish criminals."

551.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
551.text: "All Wehzek Bluds and Derdian citizens are to be turned away at the Rizian border."

552.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
552.text: "This is not strictly about Golcondism. It is about terrorists and those who support them."

553.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
553.text: "What I understand is that Bludish refugees have a fast track to Derdian citizenship. By allowing Derdian passport holders into Rizia, you may as well be opening your doors to the BFF."

554.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
554.text: "I do understand your concerns, however. I might be willing to leave Derdia out of our agreement if enough of our other conditions are met."

558.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
558.text: "These are my terms. You may take or leave them."

562.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
562.text: "I've been told that your kingdom is about to come into a large amount of natural gas. But your councilors will tell you about the importance of diversifying one's energy sources."

563.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
563.text: "You cannot get by on your natural gas stores forever. Your councilors will tell you about the importance of diversifying one's energy sources."

567.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
567.text: "Your kingdom may be about to come into a large amount of natural gas. Either way, your councilors will tell you about the importance of diversifying one's energy sources."

568.speaker: Player_Romus
568.text: "We're still on shaky ground with the Grand Duchy of Pales despite our gas agreement. Having a backup energy source might be prudent."

569.speaker: Player_Romus
569.text: "Your republic is not known for its stability. How can you guarantee that you'll be a reliable trading partner?"

570.speaker: Player_Romus
570.text: "You may be right. Access to oil alongside natural gas would grant us more flexibility, not to mention more options for trade with our neighbors."

571.speaker: Player_Romus
571.text: "Rizia already has all the energy it needs, Mr. President. We do not wish to purchase more."

572.speaker: Player_Romus
572.text: "Yes, there's no guarantee we'll be awarded any part of that gas field. Having a backup energy source might be prudent."

573.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
573.text: "Correct, Your Majesty. Until the final agreement is signed, we cannot rely on access to the Aureus field for our energy needs or any other country's."

574.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
574.text: "As long as I am president of Wehlen, the oil will keep flowing. That much, I can promise you."

575.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
575.text: "But of course, there are ways that Rizia can help Wehlen remain stable. As we have already discussed."

576.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
576.text: "Both of you are correct. Oil has uses that natural gas does not -- and vice versa."

577.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
577.text: "I will remind you all that Wehlen is under partial sanctions by most of the West."

578.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
578.text: "The one commodity they have been trading freely is oil, but the embargo we agreed on with Rumburg has been slowing that down."

585.speaker: Player_Romus
585.text: "Is the bilateral migration agreement what it sounds like?"

586.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
586.text: "And they are not acting alone. Their so-called fight for 'peace' is in reality a mass destabilization effort funded by the West."

587.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
587.text: "In fact, one of the BFF's biggest supporters is none other than your lovely sister-in-law."

588.speaker: Player_Romus
588.text: "I hope you have concrete evidence to back up that accusation, Mr. President."

589.speaker: Player_Romus
589.text: "I have no knowledge of what the Kingdom of Rumburg does or doesn't do in Wehlen."

590.speaker: Player_Romus
590.text: "Do not besmirch the honor of Her Excellency Queen Beatrice, President Smolak."

591.speaker: Player_Romus
591.text: "I beg your pardon, but I have trouble believing you. The BFF are a ragtag bunch of insurgents, not part of a Western-led conspiracy."

592.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
592.text: "We are gathering exactly such evidence. Our report on this will shock the world."

593.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
593.text: "Then perhaps you should ask Her Excellency to fill you in the next time you sit down for tea."

594.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
594.text: "There is no honor among criminals, Your Majesty."

595.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
595.text: "Believe it or don't believe it, Your Majesty. The effects of their bloody crusade will be the same."

598.speaker: Player_Romus
598.text: "No need to go on. We'll find a compromise that allows us to keep Derdia out of the ban."

599.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
599.text: "Well, Your Majesty, let's say the Republic of Wehlen decided to take a more proactive approach to the BFF problem."

601.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
601.text: "If your kingdom promised to directly aid us in that, it would of course be far more valuable than any form of border control."

602.speaker: Player_Romus
602.text: "'Proactive'? 'Problem'? I don't like the sound of either of those."

603.speaker: Player_Romus
603.text: "What kind of aid would be required?"

604.speaker: Player_Romus
604.text: "I am all for proactivity. If we don't nip terrorism in the bud now, we will pay a steep price later."

605.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
605.text: "Indeed not, President Smolak. I hope that your so-called solution does not involve retaliatory violence."

606.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
606.text: "It sounds as if the President of Wehlen is asking for the intervention of the Rizian military."

609.speaker: Player_Romus
609.text: "I don't need to hear another option. We'll include Derdia in the agreement if we need to."

610.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
610.text: "I was only trying to be helpful. But very well."

612.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
612.text: "It is our long-term goal to drive the insurgents out of their strongholds in the north of our country. Once that happens, we suspect some will flee south towards Zille."

613.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
613.text: "Were the ban limited to only those with Bludish identification documents, we would have a far easier time implementing it. Surely you understand."

614.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
614.text: "Yes! See, Wehlen and Rizia have much in common."

615.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
615.text: "What exactly are you planning, President Smolak? Do you require the services of our armed forces?"

616.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
616.text: "And in that case, we would be most grateful if the Rizian Navy actively deployed and prevented them from reaching their destination."

617.speaker: Player_Romus
617.text: "Our navy is currently preoccupied with Pales."

621.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
621.text: "I am not asking for your help today. Only someday."

622.speaker: Player_Romus
622.text: "This is your battle to fight, President Smolak. Not Rizia's."

623.speaker: Player_Romus
623.text: "I see. A small contribution towards the greater fight against terrorism."

627.speaker: Player_Romus
627.text: "You are asking too much of my country, President Smolak."

628.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
628.text: "Then I'm happy to discuss our other terms."

632.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
632.text: "But I am also happy to discuss our other terms."

633.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
633.text: "All of us must do our part in the fight against Bludish extremism and Western influence, Your Majesty."

634.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
634.text: "Wehlen and Rizia arm in arm, neutralizing the double threat of Bludish extremism and Western influence. Just imagine."

635.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
635.text: "I still have other terms to discuss.."

636.speaker: Player_Romus
636.text: "That's too good of a rate to be true. There must be a catch."

637.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
637.text: "No catch, Your Majesty. I'm just that generous of a guy."

638.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
638.text: "Even if the AN rules in our favor, we can still use oil for trade with our other neighbors."

639.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
639.text: "I will correct you there, Your Majesty. Having an energy surplus for export could prove very useful down the line."

640.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
640.text: "See, Your Majesty? Your councilors are very wise."

644.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
644.text: "But of course, there are ways that Rizia can help Wehlen remain stable. As we will discuss."

645.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
645.text: "As for your gold, I know better than to question its quality."

646.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
646.text: "But I have concerns about the consistency of your supply."

647.speaker: Player_Romus
647.text: "Nonsense, Mr. President. Our mining output is as robust as it's ever been."

651.speaker: Player_Romus
651.text: "As the owner of nearly half of Rizia's royal mining company, I have a vested interest in keeping gold production consistent."

652.speaker: Player_Romus
652.text: "As a stakeholder in Rizia's royal mining company, I have a vested interest in keeping gold production consistent."

653.speaker: Player_Romus
653.text: "Our new regulations may have slowed production temporarily, but I assure you they will be good for productivity in the long run."

659.speaker: Player_Romus
659.text: "Are you referring to Morella's talk at the AN? I hope you don't actually believe in Prime Minister Saltana's empty threats."

660.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
660.text: "Perhaps you do. But will you be able to keep Morella from nationalizing the MITZ and taking over your mines?"

661.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
661.text: "Until Morella nationalizes the MITZ and your mines vanish. I was there at the AN too, if you'll recall."

662.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
662.text: "President Smolak, please rest assured that we will not promise you an amount of gold we are unable to deliver."

663.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
663.text: "They didn't sound so empty to me, Your Majesty."

664.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
664.text: "However, we have other commodities that we can offer instead of or in addition to gold. Would those be of interest?"

665.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
665.text: "Rizia is as interested as you are in making this as fair and beneficial a deal as possible, Mr. President."

667.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
667.text: "We are asking for complete freedom of movement between Wehlen and Rizia."

668.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
668.text: "It is also our wish that Wehzeks residing in this country enjoy the same rights as native-born Rizians."

672.speaker: Player_Romus
672.text: "Wehzeks already have the same right to work as Rizians do."

673.speaker: Player_Romus
673.text: "I wish I could grant equal rights to Wehzeks. But I'm afraid my hands are tied."

674.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
674.text: "Yes, I appreciated your decree. I am sure the Rizian economy did as well."

675.speaker: Player_Romus
675.text: "Such an agreement would open the floodgates for an uncontrollable migration wave."

676.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
676.text: "There would be no 'floodgates', Your Majesty. My government is prepared to assist in the transition."

677.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
677.text: "I don't understand. The king makes the decisions, no?"

678.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
678.text: "Mr. Smolak, Mr. President, I agree that the Wehzeks who have made Zille their home should be allowed to continue living and working there. That was part of the original treaty as well."

679.speaker: Player_Romus
679.text: "I can extend those rights to the Wehzeks currently living in Zille. But to every citizen in Wehlen?"

680.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
680.text: "Everyone or no one, Your Majesty. Otherwise, those in Zille risk becoming isolated from their family and business connections on the mainland."

681.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
681.text: "From there, what I am requesting would not be such a big leap. Ability to own property, access to health care and welfare and so forth."

682.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
682.text: "Yes, yes. That's why we need to make sure all options have been laid on the table. Metaphorically speaking."

683.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
683.text: "And has the economy suffered for it? Quite the opposite, I'll wager."

684.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
684.text: "If it were highly regulated, the integration of Wehzeks into the Rizian work force could be more of a benefit than a drawback."

688.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
688.text: "If it were highly regulated, the integration of Wehzeks into the Rizian work force could be more of a benefit than a drawback."

689.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
689.text: "His Majesty has already made great strides in integrating Wehzeks into the greater Rizian workforce."

690.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
690.text: "Precisely, Mr. Esquibel. Rizians can't hold a candle to my people's work ethic."

691.speaker: Player_Romus
691.text: "I am duty-bound to wield my power in accordance with the will of the people. And I am positive the majority of Rizians oppose this."

692.speaker: Player_Romus
692.text: "I must abide by the advice of my councilors and the House of Delegates. None of whom want citizens of your country flooding mine."

693.speaker: Player_Romus
693.text: "To make such a powerful decree would be an abuse of my authority. I cannot do it without first consulting with my most trusted officials."

694.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
694.text: "With that said, Mr. Smolak, are you not worried about a potential loss of skilled workers as Wehzeks seek higher compensation in Rizia?"

695.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
695.text: "But to extend those rights to anyone coming from Wehlen... it would have to be done smoothly and carefully to avoid overloading our social services."

696.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
696.text: "There is also the concern that Wehlen will lose a great many skilled workers as they seek better compensation in Rizia."

697.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
697.text: "I beg your pardon, Mr. President, but it would be a big leap indeed. Rizia's social services are budgeted and scaled to serve our citizens alone. We can't risk overloading them."

698.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
698.text: "Of course I have thought about that. But the trade agreement I have already proposed will help level out the economic disparities between our nations."

702.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
702.text: "Of course I have thought about that. We have yet to discuss my proposed trade agreement, which I believe will help level out our nations' economic disparities."

703.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
703.text: "You asked for Wehlen's help in the past. We are only asking that the favor be returned."

704.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
704.text: "But I agree that promising any more could prove dangerous. Rizia's social services are budgeted and scaled to serve our citizens alone. We can't risk overloading them."

705.speaker: Player_Romus
705.text: "Yes, and have you considered the risks to your own country, Mr. President? Won't Wehlen lose skilled workers as they seek out higher wages in Rizia?"

706.speaker: Player_Romus
706.text: "I am still skeptical that opening up our workforce is a good idea. We accept Wehzeks as guest workers -- isn't that enough?"

707.speaker: Player_Romus
707.text: "Good point. I have nothing but compassion for the citizens of Wehlen, but Rizia will always come first."

708.speaker: Player_Romus
708.text: "That is debatable, Mr. Esquibel. The economic benefits of better integrating our two countries might offset the cost."

709.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
709.text: "And indeed, the new handover plan his ministers are now proposing has a three-year timeline attached to it."

710.speaker: Player_Romus
710.text: "Three years... that can't be standard procedure, can it?"

711.speaker: Player_Romus
711.text: "I trusted you, Mr. Esquibel. You couldn't do any better than that?"

712.speaker: Player_Romus
712.text: "Three years is nothing in the grand scheme of my lengthy reign. I am willing to wait."

713.speaker: Player_Romus
713.text: "If that's how long it takes for this to be done properly, then I'm fine with that."

714.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
714.text: "My deepest apologies, Your Majesty. As I said, this is an unprecedented situation, and I have been trying my best to find a way out of it."

715.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
715.text: "As I said, this is an unprecedented situation. I believe the AN is satisfied that President Smolak has set a new deadline at all."

716.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
716.text: "I am glad you see it that way, Your Majesty. The more desperate we seem, the more Wehlen will feel entitled to demand from us."

717.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
717.text: "I feel the same way. It's enough time for us to plan a smooth and airtight transition."

718.speaker: Lucita Azaro
718.text: "We had exactly such a smooth transition planned out. It's frankly ridiculous that we are allowing Wehlen to set the pace."

719.speaker: Lucita Azaro
719.text: "Wehlen is entitled to nothing. How do you not see that?"

721.speaker: Lucita Azaro
721.text: "And what makes us think that this one will be met when the last one was not?"

722.speaker: Narrator
722.text: Anger danced in Lucita's eyes. She gestured at the rest of the table.

723.speaker: Lucita Azaro
723.text: "This is our territory. Why are we not setting the agenda?"

727.speaker: Vina Toras
727.text: "I'm surprised the international community is not challenging an oppressive ruler like President Smolak."

728.speaker: Narrator
728.text: The others looked at her in mild surprise.

729.speaker: Vina Toras
729.text: "What of the people living in Zille? Has anyone asked them how they feel about an extra three years of Wehzek rule?"

731.speaker: Elena Werner
731.text: "We may still have the opportunity to set the agenda. Any agreement Wehlen proposes is bound to have an economic aspect."

732.speaker: Elena Werner
732.text: "And considering the dire straits Wehlen is in with the rest of the world, President Smolak might be about to offer us the deal of our lives."

736.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
736.text: "Yet you remain closely tied to Rumburg, a nation that is clearly oriented towards Arcasia and the West despite all pretenses to the contrary."
736.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Valgsland_AppealToAtANSpeech"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Morella_ANSpeech_SideWith"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Lespia_WehlenHelp"] == true) == false)

738.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
738.text: "We have economic and familial ties to Rumburg. That does not mean we share their views."

739.speaker: Narrator
739.text: President Smolak smiled just a little too widely.

740.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
740.text: "Rizia above all. I feel like I have heard that somewhere before."

741.speaker: Narrator
741.text: He scratched his head in mock confusion.

743.speaker: Player_Romus
743.text: "So you are trying to drag Rizia down to Wehlen's level."

744.speaker: Player_Romus
744.text: "It will take more than a trade deal to repair Wehlen's damage, Mr. Smolak."

745.speaker: Player_Romus
745.text: "Wehlen does have a lot of untapped potential. With the right path of development, it could be restored to the glory days of the 1920s."

746.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
746.text: "Despite the devastation in our past, we remain a country with plentiful resources, not the least of which is our people."

747.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
747.text: "If you don't see our potential, then I feel sorry for you."

748.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
748.text: "We are a diamond in the rough, Your Majesty. Set us in gold, and we will shine."

751.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
751.text: "The rest of the world may unjustly doubt Wehlen's cause. But they are ignoring our many resources. Not least of which is our people.

752.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
752.text: "No, Your Majesty. It is not 'enough' that your country has grown to rely on the cheap labor of a Wehzek underclass."

753.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
753.text: "All I am asking for is a more equal partnership. One where my citizens' contributions to your great country are valued and recognized."

755.speaker: Narrator
755.text: Laurento took one last glance at his folder, then looked up at us both.

758.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
758.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_WehlenDemands_EqualRights"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_WehlenDemands_Trade"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_WehlenDemands_NoBluds"] == true) == false

760.speaker: Player_Romus
760.text: "Not everything. What about this three-year timeline?"

761.speaker: Player_Romus
761.text: "Everything except for which of these measures will actually be implemented and how."

762.speaker: Player_Romus
762.text: "I still believe President Smolak is asking for too much. Especially in light of Wehlen's poor international standing."

763.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
763.text: "Yes, well, that's still to be decided upon."

764.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
764.text: "The timeline is to ensure that your kingdom can be relied upon, Your Majesty."

765.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
765.text: "We are looking for a long-term partnership with Rizia. You cannot simply tear up this treaty as soon as you get what you want."

766.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
766.text: "Your Majesty, any agreement we make today will go into effect as soon as possible, but the Zille handover will not."

767.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
767.text: "So we are asking for a three-year probationary period. If all is still well between Wehlen and Rizia by the end of that time, we will be able to return Zille with full confidence."

771.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
771.text: "Perhaps you're new to negotiation, Your Majesty? We start high and end up somewhere in the middle."

772.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
772.text: "You are in no position to be saying that to me, Your Majesty. But I will remain in this room out of courtesy for you and your kingdom."

773.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
773.text: "I'll remind you that any agreement we make today will go into effect as soon as possible, but the Zille handover will not."

774.speaker: Player_Romus
774.text: "Do not doubt my kingdom's ability to deliver on its promises."

775.speaker: Player_Romus
775.text: "We don't need three years. We'll get you everything you're asking for in three months."

776.speaker: Player_Romus
776.text: "When will it end? How can I be sure that three years won't turn into ten?"

777.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
777.text: "Don't worry, Your Majesty. As long as the terms are met, the handover will proceed as planned."

778.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
778.text: "Certainly not, Your Majesty. This is just a formality suggested by my ministers."

779.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
779.text: "We would prefer to have proof of Rizia's reliability in the long term."

780.speaker: Narrator
780.text: Laurento finished jotting something down on his notepad.

781.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
781.text: "Thank you for your explanations, Mr. Smolak. This has been very informative."

782.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
782.text: "Would you mind waiting in the sitting room while His Majesty and I decide on Rizia's half of the agreement?"

784.speaker: Narrator
784.text: Smolak exited the room backwards, bowing as he did so.

786.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
786.text: "Well. Quite a lot to think about, Your Majesty."

787.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
787.text: "I have the draft documents right here, if you're ready."

788.speaker: Player_Romus
788.text: "I'm ready to get this over with."

789.speaker: Player_Romus
789.text: "I have a few more questions, if you please."

791.speaker: Player_Romus
791.text: "I still feel Mr. Smolak is demanding too much."

792.speaker: Player_Romus
792.text: "What will the impact be if I enact the bans he's asking for?"

793.speaker: Player_Romus
793.text: "I'm confused about this trade deal he's asking for. Do we need to import and export exactly the same amount of goods?"

794.speaker: Player_Romus
794.text: "Granting Wehzeks full rights in Rizia... do you think that's a good idea?"

796.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
796.text: "Tighter immigration controls would overjoy your nationalist supporters."

801.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
801.text: "You have a significant negotiating edge over Wehlen. However, President Smolak is still expecting a conciliatory gesture, even if only a small symbolic one."

802.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
802.text: "To be honest, we don't have enough of a negotiating edge over Wehlen to simply discard this agreement."

803.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
803.text: "If you refuse every single one of the conditions listed here, a diplomatic handover of Zille will be out of the question."

804.speaker: Player_Romus
804.text: "In other words, we'll have to resort to one of those contingency plans we discussed earlier."

810.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
810.text: "As Derdians also fill many low-wage jobs in Rizia, the ban may dent our economy as well."

811.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
811.text: "But refusing Derdians entry into our country would lead to an outcry both internationally and from our existing Derdian population."

812.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
812.text: "The ban on Bluds should not ruffle as many feathers. Though if the rumors concerning Rumburg's support of the BFF are true, we do risk raising the ire of Her Excellency."

813.speaker: Player_Romus
813.text: "I appreciate your efforts to keep the peace. But even you must realize that a diplomatic handover was never in the cards. Not as long as that guy's in charge of Wehlen."

814.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
814.text: "I know President Smolak is an eccentric man. But I do believe his primary intention is to end Wehlen's isolation."

815.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
815.text: "I suppose so. I must warn you, those could end up costing us far more dearly than a few trade and border concessions."

817.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
817.text: "If he feels he has an ally in Rizia, there will be no reason for him to keep control of Zille."

820.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
820.text: "As a matter of fact, we're in a position to make a very advantageous deal. Especially if we meet the President's other demands."

821.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
821.text: "In fact, if we don't want to make too many concessions in other areas, we may have to settle for a lopsided deal."

825.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
825.text: "It is perhaps President Smolak's boldest demand."

826.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
826.text: "However, your decree to grant migrants the right to work in all sectors has already opened the door for it somewhat."

827.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
827.text: "And it would be a rather extreme leap for Rizia, considering that Wehzeks and other migrants do not even have the right to work the same jobs native-born Rizians do."

831.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
831.text: "And your decision to fund a Dastnurist sanctuary shows that you respect Wehzeks' right to practice their religion in this country."

832.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
832.text: "Passing such a monumental decree without the approval of your council or the House of Delegates could prove dangerous."

833.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
833.text: "At least your decision to fund a Dastnurist sanctuary shows that you respect Wehzeks' right to practice their religion in this country. That should count for something."

837.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
837.text: "Granting working rights is the furthest you should go, I think. But other factions may have different opinions."

838.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
838.text: "Expanding on that without the approval of your council or the House of Delegates could prove dangerous. But it would certainly be possible."

839.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
839.text: "Of course, you should still be wary of backlash from certain nationalist factions. You'd do well to curry favor with your uncle's side of the family."

858.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
858.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_WehlenDemandAddtlQs_SayNo"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_WehlenDemandAddtlQs_Ban"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_WehlenDemandAddtlQs_Trade"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_WehlenDemandAddtlQs_Rights"] == true

859.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
859.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_WehlenDemandAddtlQs_SayNo"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_WehlenDemandAddtlQs_Ban"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_WehlenDemandAddtlQs_Trade"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_WehlenDemandAddtlQs_Rights"] == true) == false

860.speaker: Player_Romus
860.text: "Thank you, Mr. Esquibel. Let's have a look at the draft."
860.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_WehlenDemandAddtlQs_SayNo"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_WehlenDemandAddtlQs_Ban"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_WehlenDemandAddtlQs_Trade"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_WehlenDemandAddtlQs_Rights"] == true

861.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
861.text: "Think of everyone in Zille, Your Majesty. We are doing this for them."

863.speaker: Narrator
863.text: He handed me the treaty amendment draft, and I began going through it.

865.speaker: Narrator
865.text: Laurento noted each decision I made in the margins of the document. When we had finished going through everything, he sat back and raised an eyebrow.

869.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
869.text: "I should have expected nothing less from you, King Romus."

873.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
873.text: "Very bold, Your Majesty. I hope Wehlen will accept it."

877.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
877.text: "Wehlen should have no trouble accepting this, Your Majesty. The question is, will Rizia?"

878.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
878.text: "This all seems reasonable, Your Majesty. I hope Wehlen sees it that way as well."

879.speaker: Narrator
879.text: He asked an aide to call Smolak back into the room.

881.speaker: Narrator
881.text: The President of Wehlen wiped rizetta crumbs off of his mustache as he entered.

882.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
882.text: "What a delicious tart your people have invented! Now imagine it with a crust made of our strudel pastry..."

883.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
883.text: "But first things first. Let's have a look at that treaty."

884.speaker: Narrator
884.text: Laurento handed him the annotated draft, and he flipped through it eagerly.

885.speaker: Narrator
885.text: As he reached the end, his eyes filled with fury.

893.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
893.text: "Despite the effort my ministers have spent on this draft, despite the time I took to come to your country, despite the horrific act of violence against my citizens..."

894.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
894.text: "You have chosen to ignore every last one of my demands."

895.speaker: Narrator
895.text: As he reached the end, his eyes narrowed.

897.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
897.text: "I was not aware that the King of Rizia took me for a simpleton."

898.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
898.text: "Assuming, of course, that you are planning on fulfilling these promises."

899.speaker: Narrator
899.text: As he reached the end, his eyes filled with glee.

903.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
903.text: "We can definitely work with this, Your Majesty."

904.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
904.text: "I have to say, I was not expecting such generosity from you."

905.speaker: Player_Romus
905.text: "Apologies, Mr. President, but I simply cannot promise you more than this."

906.speaker: Player_Romus
906.text: "What are you talking about? This is the best deal you're going to get."

907.speaker: Player_Romus
907.text: "Let's try to behave like gentlemen, Mr. Smolak. Lashing out will not solve anything."

908.speaker: Player_Romus
908.text: "My deepest apologies, but I simply cannot agree to what you are asking."

909.speaker: Player_Romus
909.text: "That act of violence was not my responsibility. Why should Rizia atone for crimes it didn't commit?"

911.speaker: Player_Romus
911.text: "It was not my intention to waste your government's time, Mr. President."

912.speaker: Player_Romus
